chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfaly, from al-Fadl ibn Yunus, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) had lunch with me, so a bowl was brought with bread underneath it. He said: 'Honor the bread, so that it should not be under the bowl.' And he said to me: 'Instruct the servant to take the loaf out from beneath the bowl.'

key_terms.تَغَدَّى: had lunch / had a midday meal

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette regarding placing bread on the ground according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual etiquette of honoring sustenance by preventing bread from touching the ground directly. This practice reflects the Shia tradition of treating food as a divine blessing, linking physical cleanliness with spiritual gratitude and humility in daily consumption.
